name: RIPEMD-160 outside the reference’s reachable domain
rule: Every digest below was returned by MochimoHasher.hashWith("ripemd160"), which delegates to @noble/hashes. Every input is emitted as bytes beside the digest. Nothing here is hand-computed and nothing is transcribed except the one published digest, which the generator verifies and aborts on. Regenerate rather than edit.

oracle.why: Two independent implementations of a PUBLISHED algorithm, neither of which is the specification for the other: @noble/hashes here, and RustCrypto’s ripemd in native::ripemd160. That is error detection rather than conformance, and it is a stronger relationship than group C’s, where the C is the specification. What it is NOT is evidence about Mochimo: nothing Mochimo-specific is computed in this file.
oracle.why_not_group_cx: Group CX records a second implementation’s answer to a question the C already answered. For this input class the C answers nothing -- ripemd160_final overflows its stack and the process dies. Filing these in CX would make CX’s own oracle statement false of some of its members, and a group whose claim holds for only part of its contents is how a distinction erodes.
oracle.domain: Every length in 0..=200 with len % 64 >= 56 -- 24 lengths, residues 56..=63 at three successive block counts, so the overflowing store is exercised as the first block, after one full block, and after several. Plus every member of RIPEMD-160’s published test suite whose length satisfies the same predicate -- the WHOLE suite is carried and filtered, so the qualifying count is an output of the predicate rather than a list somebody curated. Two qualify, at 56 and 62 bytes. Both counts are asserted by the generator, which also executes every published digest including the ones that never reach this file. See errata 70.
oracle.disclosure: Disclosure status for this defect is recorded in errata 52 (docs/errata.md), which is the authoritative copy. It is not restated here: six sites carried independent copies until R5 and each needed correcting separately when the status changed. The defect itself is unfixed, which is why this group exists; that is a different fact from its disclosure status and the two moved separately.

vectors.note: RIPEMD-160 of 56 bytes. 56 % 64 = 56, which is >= 56, so ripemd160_final takes its two-block branch and writes past a one-block buffer. The vendored C cannot produce this digest; it dies producing it.
vectors.falsifies: that native::ripemd160 is unverified on the faulting class. It is not verified against the reference -- that is impossible -- but against an independent implementation of the same published algorithm
vectors.reference_cannot_compute_reason: ripemd160.c:170-183 overflows uint8_t final[64] for this length class (docs/errata.md entry 52). Calling the reference here terminates the process, so there is no reference value to record and no way to obtain one without patching the reference.

vectors.note: the 56-byte overlapping-quadruples string. ADDED IN P3-6: it was absent from this array while errata 52 recorded its length as 64, which put it outside the faulting class it is in. Errata 70. Its length is 56, so 56 % 64 = 56 and it lands INSIDE the faulting class. The vendored RIPEMD-160 therefore cannot compute one of RIPEMD-160's own published test vectors -- which is the single most legible statement of the defect available.
